comments.body: Disposition change: this is NO LONGER deferred — it is being fixed together with parent 1137 in the same change (Gerrit #2399). Rationale: the plan-review gate on 1137 (LLM Pass, finding G6) flagged that fixing attest.py while leaving drift_floor.py:126's byte-identical unscoped head_sha read would leave two 'intentionally synchronized' stale-head anchors that could diverge. Rather than mirror the fix inline (re-introducing synchronized-by-copy fragility), we extracted a single shared helper gate_source.current_head_sha(auth_manifest, repo_root) that BOTH attest._unscoped_head_drift and drift_floor's code_drifted block now read, so they cannot diverge. drift_floor now catches SnapshotError -> 'unknown' (denies convergence, never suppresses findings — honoring drift_floor's own 'a broken signal can only DENY convergence, never suppress incorrectly' contract). Teeth tests added in tests/unit/test_plan_review_drift_floor.py (candidate reads the shared gate-ref anchor not the working tree; denies convergence when gate ref unresolvable). Will close this ticket once #2399 merges (Verified +1).

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/drift_floor.py:126` (`drift_floor_candidate`) computes the
drift-refresh eligibility `code_drifted` reason as:

```python
signed_sha = signing.verified_at_sha_from_manifest(manifest)   # the GATE-REF sha at review time
current_sha = signing.head_sha(_config.repo_root(repo_root))    # git rev-parse HEAD of the working tree
reasons["code_drifted"] = bool(signed_sha) and bool(current_sha) and current_sha != "unknown" and signed_sha != current_sha
```

This is the SAME defect class as bug `1137-8215-ec04-4ca0` (seaworthy-revengeful-blobfish): it
compares the signed **gate-ref** sha (`verified_at_sha`) against `git rev-parse HEAD` of whatever
working tree the evaluator sits in. Its own comment states it "mirrors compute_validity's unscoped
whole-HEAD 'stale-head' trigger anchor **exactly**" — and 1137's fix corrected compute_validity's
unscoped trigger to resolve the CURRENT gate ref (via `resolve_ref(default_ref, working, fetch=False)`,
`source=local`/legacy tolerant, fail-closed on unresolvable). This site was NOT updated, so it now
DIVERGES from the invariant its comment asserts.

## Impact (why this is P3, not P2)
Unlike 1137 this does NOT block claims. `drift_floor_candidate` is the drift-refresh REUSE floor: a
spurious `code_drifted=True` only DENIES cheap-refresh eligibility, forcing a (safe but wasteful)
FULL re-review, and makes `_drifted_paths(signed_sha, current_sha)` diff the gate-ref sha against a
FOREIGN commit (bogus drifted-file lists). Conservative/wasteful, not incorrect-blocking.

## Non-trivial subtlety (DO NOT fix blind)
drift_floor's failure semantics DIFFER from attest.py's: `code_drifted` guards `current_sha != "unknown"`,
so an UNRESOLVABLE current sha reads as NOT drifted → **fail-OPEN** (would reuse a possibly-stale review).
attest.py fails CLOSED on the same condition. A correct fix must resolve the current gate-ref sha AND
handle resolution failure so it does not introduce a fail-open drift-refresh reuse. This needs its own
RED->GREEN test (attested manifest, origin/main unmoved, foreign working-tree HEAD -> code_drifted must
be False/eligible; gate ref moved -> code_drifted True; gate ref unresolvable -> conservative not-eligible).

## Suggested approach
Mirror 1137's attest.py fix: resolve `resolve_ref(gate_source.default_ref(working), working, fetch=False)`
for attested manifests (source=local / no-verified_at_sha keep head_sha), and map a SnapshotError to a
conservative not-eligible outcome (NOT eligible), preserving drift_floor's fail-safe direction. Consider a
shared helper with attest.py's `_unscoped_head_drift` so the documented mirror invariant holds by construction.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `drift_floor_candidate` resolves the CURRENT gate ref (not working-tree HEAD) for attested manifests.
- [ ] source=local and no-verified_at_sha manifests keep the working-tree basis (unchanged).
- [ ] Gate-ref resolution failure yields a CONSERVATIVE not-eligible outcome (no fail-open reuse).
- [ ] RED->GREEN test proves the foreign-working-tree false-drift is gone and moved/unresolvable ref semantics preserved.
- [ ] Mirror invariant with compute_validity's unscoped trigger restored (ideally a shared helper).
compiled_state.title: drift_floor_candidate reads working-tree HEAD, not the gate ref, for attested code-drift eligibility (1137 sibling)
